title: Honor your friends (Berakhot 28b)
hookLine: Rabbi Eliezer's students ask for life's paths; he answers: be careful of your friends' honor
tomorrow: his students call him the lamp of Israel. so why is he crying?

cards: Graduation speakers get a few minutes to tell a room what matters most. Rabbi Eliezer gets a harder version. He's sick in bed, his students come to visit, and they ask him: teach us the paths of life.
His first answer isn't about prayer, and it isn't about study. It's this: be careful with your friends' honor.

teach.b: He goes on. Keep your children from higayon, a word readers explain in different ways. Seat them at the knees of the sages.
And when you pray, know before whom you stand.
Four paths, and the friend comes first.
Now look back at this week, because it kept circling the same place. Mar's own prayer asked God to guard his tongue. Rava called himself dust while alive.
The sages of Yavneh said much or little, the heart, and wouldn't look down on the man in the field. Rav's world to come had no jealousy and no competition.
Then Gamliel shamed one student, the doors opened, and he walked to Joshua's house to ask forgiveness. Rabbi Eliezer's first path is where all of it lands.
A friend's honor is easy to break and worth guarding, and it's yours to guard. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight.

teach.h: START WITH WHO'S NEXT TO YOU.
teach.b: Asked for the way to the world to come, a sage didn't start with heaven.
He started with the people sitting next to you.

how: Jewish teaching counts guarding another person's dignity as a serious duty, and students of the Talmud often learn Rabbi Eliezer's four paths of life together as a short list to live by.

o: put your teachers' needs ahead of your friends'
guard the dignity of the people closest to you
choose your friends only from the study hall

games.q: Rabbi Eliezer's paths — tap the pairs.
p: seat them at the sages' knees
a word read in different ways

s: Rabbi Eliezer's first path of life is about prayer
his first answer: be careful with your friends' honor. prayer comes last.
this week's sages kept coming back to how people treat each other
Mar's guarded tongue, the Yavneh field worker, Gamliel's walk to Joshua's house.

games.q: at a party, an old embarrassing video of your friend starts going around. what does Rabbi Eliezer's first path ask of you?
o: guard her honor: don't pass it on, and stand with her.
laugh along; it's harmless if everyone is already sharing it.
stay out of it; her honor is only her own business.
games.why: be careful with your friends' honor: in Berakhot 28b, it's the first path of life, and it's yours to guard.

practice: Count on your fingers the friends who've been good to you lately, one finger each. For each one, name a single thing about them worth honoring. If one name stings because you owe them something, hold that finger a little longer.

wordCard.voice: Honor your friends. Rabbi Eliezer's first path of life, said from a sickbed: be careful with your friends' honor.

orig.note: Hebrew: be careful with the honor of your friends. Rabbi Eliezer's first path of life.

carryVoice: Carry this: honor your friends, a sage's first path to the world to come. Eighteen of fifty, and a week of Berakhot behind you.
